comparison: cover crop vs. bare fallow or winter weeds
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled, not corn/soybean specific)
quote: The modeled change across all management types and all sites was + 10.9% [95% CI: 7.5–14.5] for yield (Fig. 3A) and + 9.8% [95% CI: 7.0–12.6] for SOC (Fig. 4A).
note: Pooled across all cash crops (grain and fruit, e.g. tomatoes, cotton); no separate corn or soybean estimate reported. Preprint of Vendig et al. 2023 Nature Sustainability.

comparison: legume cover crop vs. bare fallow, continuous cash crop monoculture
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled)
quote: Holding all else at its average, ΔYield in legume cover crop treatments was significantly greater in continuous cash crop monocultures (+ 21.0%, 95% CI: 15.0–27.3) versus rotations with two (+ 9.3%, 95% CI: 1.7–17.5) cash crop species (Fig. 3B).
note: Moderator: rotational complexity. For 3+ cash crops in rotation, legume effect not different from zero.

comparison: legume cover crop vs. bare fallow, two-crop rotation
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled)
quote: Holding all else at its average, ΔYield in legume cover crop treatments was significantly greater in continuous cash crop monocultures (+ 21.0%, 95% CI: 15.0–27.3) versus rotations with two (+ 9.3%, 95% CI: 1.7–17.5) cash crop species (Fig. 3B).
note: Two-crop rotation (e.g. corn-soybean type systems, though crops not specified).

comparison: non-legume cover crop vs. bare fallow, 3+ cash crops in rotation
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled)
quote: At the average level of N fertilization in our dataset, non-legume cover crops significantly increased yield only in plots with 3 or more cash crops in rotation (+ 19.2%, 95% CI: 6.9–33.0) (Fig. 3C).
note: Non-legume effects in monoculture (+5.1%, CI -1.0-11.5) and two-crop rotations (+4.5%, CI -3.3-12.9) overlapped zero.

comparison: legume cover crop vs. bare fallow, low N (12.9 kg N ha-1 season-1)
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled)
quote: Legume cover crops in low N systems (12.9 kg N ha− 1 season− 1, one standard deviation below the mean N fertilization of our dataset) increased yield by + 17.8% (95% CI: 11.3–24.7) and in average N systems (85.9 kg N ha− 1 season− 1) increased yield by + 10.6% (95% CI: 4.8–16.8) (Fig. 3D).
note: Moderator: N fertilization. Above 136 kg N ha-1 season-1 legume effect not significant.

comparison: non-legume cover crop vs. bare fallow, average N (85.9 kg N ha-1 season-1)
metric: cash crop yield change (all cash crops pooled)
quote: Non-legume cover crops provided yield increases in low (+ 7.5%, 95% CI: 0.9–14.4), average (+ 9.4%, 95% CI: 3.0–16.2), and high (+ 11.4%, 95% CI: 3.7–19.6) N systems (Fig. 3E).
